To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the non-classical human leucocyte antigens HLA-E, HLA-F and HLA-G are important biomarkers in transplantation and tumors and that HLA-G and/or HLA-E are potential therapeutic targets for enhancing tolerance in transplantation and for enhancing immunogenicity of HLA-G expressing tumors.
HLA-G and other non-classical HLA antigens are important for immune tolerance in transplantation as well as for immune evasion in tumor cells and that they might represent novel therapeutic targets.
the non-classical HLA-G molecule is an important player in the induction of immune tolerance in the transplantation and tumor settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of HLA-G expression, function, and regulation in tumor cells and transplanted cells.
the identification of HLA-G as a promising biomarker for diagnosis and prognosis of tumors as well as a potential target for immunotherapeutic interventions.
the identification of HLA-G as a novel target for immunotherapy of cancer and transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HLA-G and the HLA-G-specific molecules are important diagnostic and prognostics biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for the treatment of transplantation and tumor diseases.
HLA-G and/or HLA-E are important for tumor and transplantation tolerance and thus might represent interesting biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
HLA-G is involved in the maintenance of immune tolerance in physiological as well as pathophysiological conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonclassical antigens HLA-G and -E represent interesting diagnostic and prognostico biomarkers and therapeutic targets in transplantation as well as in tumors.
HLA-G represents an important molecule for tolerance induction in transplants and tumor immune escape.
HLA-G is a tolerogenic molecule that can be exploited in the context of transplantation and tumor immunotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HLA-G represents an attractive target for immunotherapy in the context of transplantation and tumors.
HLA-G is a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of tumors and transplantation.

the non-classical HLA class I antigens HLA-G and -E represent promising biomarkers for the diagnosis of transplant rejection and tumors, and that these antigens are potential therapeutic targets for the induction of transplant tolerance and tumor eradication.
